articles.description:
In the previous article, we built DES from scratch — not because it’s still relevant, but because it forces you to understand how block ciphers are assembled from specifications.
DES is awkward, bit-heavy, and full of historical baggage.
That’s exactly why it’s a good learning tool.
AES continues that journey — but with very different design goals and very different failure modes.
Where DES teaches structure,
AES teaches discipline.
Before touching code, let’s be honest about one thing:
AES is not interesting because it’s new.
It’s interesting because it’s everywhere.
Right now, AES is used in:
HTTPS (TLS)
Disk encryption (BitLocker, FileVault, LUKS)
Password managers
Cloud storage
Mobile devices
VPNs
Hardware security modules
If data is encrypted in 2025, there’s a very high chance AES is…

articles.author: shubham khatik
articles.description:
The Problem
I created a 7-Phase Roadmap tailored to build a mental model step-by-step. This order ensures that every new topic uses tools you mastered in the previous phase.
🏗️ Phase 1: Basic Linear Structures & Their Patterns Goal: Mastering sequential data and index manipulation. Before touching complex nodes, master the line.
🔍 Phase 2: The Power of Lookup (Hashing)Goal: Trading space for speed.
🔗 Phase 3: Pointers & Recursion Goal: Moving from Indexes to References.
🌳 Phase 4: Non-Linear Structures (Hierarchical)Goal: Parent-Child relationships.
🕵️ Phase 5: Advanced Search & BacktrackingGoal: Exploring all possibilities.
🌐 Phase 6: Connectivity (Graphs)Goal: Many-to-Many relationships.
🚀 Phase 7: Optimization (The Hardest Part)Goal: Solving overlapping sub-problems.
Save this roadmap and stop getting lost in the noise! 🚀

Most consumer tech focuses on performance: faster, stronger, bigger numbers.
But some of the best products I’ve used recently focus on something else entirely — feedback.

After brushing, the app shows:
how evenly you brushed
whether you used too much pressure

What I like most is that it doesn’t try to change your routine.
Over a few weeks, I noticed:
less gum irritation
more even brushing coverage
fewer rushed sessions
Another smart detail: instead of pushing subscriptions, it rewards consistency.
Good tech doesn’t need to shout.
Sometimes, it just needs to show you what you’re missing.
